newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures gain on NYMEX, fresh Iraqi rumours.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures gain on NYMEX, fresh Iraqi rumours.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures gained in quiet mid-afternoon trade on NYMEX strength and uncertainty over Iraqi oil supplies, brokers said.
At 1530 gmt August Brent was up 20 cents at $17.96, 14 cents up in an hour, while July gas oil paper was down $1 at $161.75 a tonne.
Dealers differed on why Brent had lifted, though most pointed to New York business, where front month NYMEX crude was up 32 cents at $19.14.
"New York has given things a lift and there are fresh rumours of Iraqi intransigence as well," said one dealer.
Fund buyers were believed to be shorting August paper in New York to buy July paper, ahead to that contract's expiry this week, with the bidding helping prices upwards, dealers said.

Earlier, quiet trading was blamed on a lull after hectic pre-expiry activity on the IPE's Brent July paper last Friday. And Monday's upturn was only thinly supported, dealers reported, with volume low.

Some of London's rise was attributed to a fresh wave of rumours on Iraq's attitude towards the technicalities of food distribution that are holding up the restart of exports under the second oil-for-food deal with the United Nations.
